mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% over the next month, investors anticipate tighter policy, which initially suppresses equity valuations, but the anticipated future growth in rates offsets this, yielding positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite FEDFUNDS up move; or the increase is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in PAYEMS (labor market strength) above 140,000 monthly suggests robust employment, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when PAYEMS crosses above 140,000; or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (goods demand) grows by at least 5% over the prior quarter, it indicates resilient consumer spending, which elevates earnings growth forecasts and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite GDPC1 >5% quarterly growth; or the effect is not significant in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 112 suggests supply-side constraints, which can lead to upward equity valuation pressure as growth expectations are revised lower, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when INDPRO is below 112; or the effect is not robust across regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls by more than 0.2 percentage points over the next 3 months, it signals labor market strengthening, prompting risk-on sentiment and positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly positive despite UNRATE decline; or the signal is spurious in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both HOUST (housing starts) and PAYEMS (labor) above 1,200 and 145,000 respectively indicates dual recovery in housing and employment, which amplifies optimism and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
regime_hint: dual recovery in housing and labor markets
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive when both proxies cross thresholds simultaneously; or interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 4.0%), a sustained monthly increase in RSAFS (short-term Treasury demand) above 400 billion indicates risk appetite for safe assets, which is associated with positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4.0% and RSAFS > 400B for the current month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not positive when both conditions hold; or interaction is not significant in out-of-sample.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 1% in a month, it reflects inflation pressures that, if persistent, can erode equity valuations through higher discount rates, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >1% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative when CPIAUCSL >1% increase; or the effect is absent in high-inflation regimes.
